title: Tarrasch Defense: the main line
line: Black gets a lone pawn on d5, and open lines for its pieces in return.

steps.text: The Tarrasch Defense: Black strikes at White's center pawn at once.
The pawns trade on d5, and White brings out its other knight.
Bring the knight out. It adds pressure on the pawn on d4.
steps.after: White's bishop will aim at the pawn on d5 from the long diagonal.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It guards your center pawn.
Bring the bishop out so that you can castle.
Castle. Your king is safe before the center opens up.
steps.after: White's bishop pins your knight to the bishop on e7. The knight guards the pawn on d5.

steps.text: Trade pawns on d4. It opens lines for your pieces.

also.c8e6: That guards the pawn on d5, another main line. This lesson trades first.

steps.after: Your pawn on d5 stands alone now: no pawn beside it can guard it. White will aim at it.

steps.text: Push the pawn on h7 one square to ask the bishop on g5 to decide.
Put the rook on the e-file, where Black has no pawn.

also.c8g4: Bringing the bishop out is sound too. This lesson moves the rook first.

steps.after: This is the main line. White aims at the pawn on d5, and Black plays with its pieces.

summary: Black accepts a lone center pawn. It can be attacked, but it gives every Black piece room and open lines.
